blocks.text: Despite the earlier warning, sections of the Khalsa continue after the broken enemy and turn the retreat into a running night pursuit. They fall upon the fleeing Durrani troops at midnight, seize horses, weapons, and baggage, and keep the pressure on until the whole countryside feels the panic of defeat.

By dawn the chase has reached the approaches to Jalandhar, where plundered columns and scattered survivors spread alarm through the city. The Khalsa strips the roads and outer quarters so aggressively that Jalandhar appealed to Dina Beg for protection through payment before the city should be fully sacked.

The page therefore turns battlefield victory into political leverage. What began as a pursuit becomes a coercive demonstration that neither the Durrani fugitives nor the people of Jalandhar can ignore the power of the victorious Khalsa.
